questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the courses given at the host university, plus the fact that arranging through erasmus and fixed arrangements through my uni made it more easy and transparant

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: parts of it were good, though I found that it was harder to get assistance throughout the semester because my campus is so far away (and different from) the main university at AUC

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were picked up at the airport and attended 4 days orientation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I found most of the orientation unnecessary, not very oriented around the students actually getting to know each other, and quite irrelevant for me, as I and my class wouldn't go on to have classes at the main campus

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used a broker (name removed by UCPH) who was very helpful. His fee is half of 1 months rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is recommended, as the main campus in new cairo is very isolated from the rest of the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It worked well

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Director of the ALIN program was very helpful. I didn't find the International Office (IPSO) at the main campus very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No problems here

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the employees at the ALIN program rather than the IPSO office

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good, but I had hoped it would have been more intense eg. with more homework

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the levels in the courses "Media" and "Reading and Writing" was appropriate for my level, though the level was too low in MSA and ECA. I would recommend that all students from UCPH who have done the same amount of arabic classes at UCPH as I have (45 ECTS) should at least be placed in upper intermediate in MSA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It worked really well in Media and Reading and Writing. ECA was a bit slow and ineffective, though that may just be normal in an elementary class. The style of teaching in MSA wasn't suitable for my at auc, I prefered it at UCPH, where we would analyse full texts and use multiple grammar at once in the analysis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ALIN 2101-2102-2103-2104  -  Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
ALIN 2131-2132  -  Intermediate Printed and Aural Media
ALIN 2121-2122  -  Exploring Arabic through Texts: Reading and Writing
ALIN 2301-2302  -  Intermediate Colloquial Arabic

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do "ALIN 2151-2152 Exploring Arabic: Language, Identity, and Culture - With Focus on Listening and Speaking" myself, but it is my impression that the other students in my class, who took it, benefited greatly from it

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: We didn't have a functioning kitchen and didn't live close to affordable restaurants, so I was surprised by how much I've spend on food everyday

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Concerts and nightlife. Also, it is mandatory to pay for a health insurance at AUC, which I didn't know about upon arrival

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are plenty opportunities, but they are all situated at the new campus, which is 1,5 hours away from my campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are plenty opportunities, but they are all situated at the new campus, which is 1,5 hours away from my campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't use them as they were so far away

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Weekendtrips to Alexandria, Tunis Village in Fayoum, Ismailia, Ain Soukna
Longer trips to Dahab (including hiking the Sinai mountain) and Siwa
Day pass or membership at the private sports clubs such as Gezira club and Al Ahli in Zamalek 
Vintage clothes at Maspero Market (by the metro station)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, I loved living there

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As I wasn't at the main campus, I found it difficult to meet local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Though I rarely was uncomfortable, it was very different being a woman walking the streets there because of comments and staring

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The openness! It is a people who is so curious about you, each other and the world. 
Also, it was really special to experience ramadan and coptic easter there. It is such a diverse and multicultural city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live off campus! And try to avoid apartments in expat areas like Zamalek and Maadi - it's expensive and doesn't really reflect the rest of the city
Use the Add/Drop week for classes! I didn't and i ended up in a level of MSA that was too easy
Do ECA classes outside of school, most of the communication with locals in everyday life is in arabic

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Filuca-parties (parties on a boat on the Nile) are a great way of getting to know people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in downtown Cairo! It is just such a cool city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it frustration being at the wrong level in some classes. Also I didn't think the orientation week did a good job establishing good social conditions for us af the Tahrir campus. I found that I mostly just hung out with the people I met in class

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
